description: Eagerly clear the durable .cam-implement-blocked marker on the successful complete terminal and on ship-merge so it no longer orphans (cry-wolf boot blocker) after in-cycle recovery.

userStories.title: Clear implement-blocked marker on the complete terminal (loop.ts + host.ts)
userStories.description: As the orchestrator, I need the durable .cam-implement-blocked marker removed when the supervisor reaches a successful 'complete' terminal for the current issue, so that an in-cycle recovery (blocked -> retry -> DONE) does not leave an orphaned marker that false-alarms as an 'implement blocked' boot blocker.
acceptanceCriteria: loop.ts finishTerminal('complete') removes the implement-blocked marker for the current issue via a newly injected removeImplementBlockedMarkerFn, guarded by lastIssueNumber !== undefined, mirroring the existing writeImplementBlockedMarkerFn injection. [oracle: grep -q 'removeImplementBlockedMarkerFn' src/supervisor/loop.ts]

loop.ts stays filesystem/path-free: the new fn defaults to a no-op (?? (() => {})) and no fs import or path construction is added to loop.ts. [oracle: ! grep -qE "from '(node:fs|node:path)'|require\('node:fs'\)" src/supervisor/loop.ts]

The clear fires ONLY on the 'complete' terminal, not on 'blocked'/'awaiting-operator'/'max-iterations': a blocked terminal still writes and preserves the marker and the escalated circuit-breaker read path is unchanged. [oracle: bun test]

src/supervisor/host.ts wires the production removeImplementBlockedMarkerFn to removeImplementBlockedMarker(implementBlockedMarkerPath), the same path used by the existing writer. [oracle: grep -q 'removeImplementBlockedMarkerFn' src/supervisor/host.ts]
advanceBlockedMarker, the marker schema, sweepOrphanedImplementBlockedMarker, and the re-arm clear (clearImplementBlockedMarkerForCurrentIssue) are left unchanged. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]

New unit/wiring tests cover complete-terminal clear with issueId match AND the lastIssueNumber-undefined mismatch guard (no clear), plus a plain 'blocked' terminal still preserving the marker. [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/supervisor/loop.ts (finishTerminal at ~line 827; the 'complete' path calls finishTerminal('complete') at ~line 938; writeImplementBlockedMarkerFn default at ~786, lastIssueNumber at ~795 set at ~898), src/supervisor/host.ts (writer wiring at ~704-718, removeImplementBlockedMarker already importable from src/supervisor/implement-blocked-marker.ts export at line 167, implementBlockedMarkerPath at ~711, opts passed at ~1096). removeImplementBlockedMarker(filePath) takes only the path and silently no-ops when the file is absent; the issueId guard is the CALLER's responsibility here it is lastIssueNumber !== undefined (the marker written on this cycle's blocked terminal is by-construction this issue's). Mirror the finishTerminal wrapper pattern (patterns.md line ~400, CAM-188): the new fn goes inside finishTerminal alongside the existing writeImplementBlockedMarkerFn stamp, gated on status === 'complete'. Do NOT reset the escalated circuit-breaker. Ordering: autoShipFn fires BEFORE finishTerminal('complete') already; leave that ordering intact. Test-quality invariant: exercise the real finishTerminal seam via injected fns and assert the injected remove fn is/ isn't called per terminal kind (not a tautological mock-only assertion; pair with a real behavioral outcome where feasible).

userStories.title: Clear implement-blocked marker on the ship merge terminal (sidecar.ts)
userStories.description: As the orchestrator, I need the durable .cam-implement-blocked marker removed at the merge-watch 'merged' terminal when it belongs to the just-shipped issue, so that an issue which recovered in-cycle and then shipped no longer leaves an orphaned marker that false-alarms at future boots.
acceptanceCriteria: sidecar.ts merge-watch 'merged' terminal reads the implement-blocked marker and removes it only when marker.issueId === state.issueId, mirroring updateShipStalledMarker's consume-on-merge read-then-compare-then-remove pattern. [oracle: grep -q 'state.issueId' src/commands/sidecar.ts]
No removal occurs when the marker's issueId differs from state.issueId or when the marker is absent (read returns null). [oracle: bun test]
The read + issueId compare happens BEFORE calling removeImplementBlockedMarker, exactly as updateShipStalledMarker does; nothing throws when the marker file is absent. [oracle: bun test]

The change is additive: updateShipStalledMarker, updatePostMergeStalledMarker, sweepOrphanedImplementBlockedMarker, and clearImplementBlockedMarkerForCurrentIssue are unchanged. [oracle: reviewer-judgment]
New unit tests cover merged-terminal clear for the match case, the issueId-mismatch case (no clear), and the absent-marker case (no throw, no clear). [oracle: bun test]
Typecheck passes (bun run typecheck). [oracle: bun run typecheck]
Lint spine passes (bun run check:all). [oracle: bun run check:all]
userStories.notes: Files: src/commands/sidecar.ts (merge-watch 'merged' terminal at ~948-954 where updateShipStalledMarker / updatePostMergeStalledMarker already fire; readImplementBlockedMarker + removeImplementBlockedMarker + IMPLEMENT_BLOCKED_FILENAME already imported at line 56). Build the marker path as join(claudeDir, IMPLEMENT_BLOCKED_FILENAME) like the read fn factory at ~1030. state.issueId is a string|null (see updateShipStalledMarker at ~759 issueId: state.issueId ?? null); marker.issueId is a string. Guard: only when both present AND equal. Mirror updateShipStalledMarker (src/release/merge-watch.ts precedent, patterns.md line ~438/510 consume-on-merge) exactly: read, compare identity, then remove; never-throws. Do NOT touch the non-merged terminals (owned by updateShipStalledMarker) or the post-merge marker. Independent of US-001 (different seam) but ordered second; can be picked in either order.
